verdicts.title: General notions of depth for functional data
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: A data depth measures the centrality of a point with respect to an empirical distribution. Postulates are formulated, which a depth for functional data should satisfy, and a general approach is proposed to construct multivariate data depths in Banach spaces. The new approach, mentioned as Phi-depth, is based on depth infima over a proper set Phi of R^d-valued linear functions. verdicts.title: On the Hilbert depth of quadratic and cubic functions
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Given a numerical function $h:\mathbb Z_{\geq 0}\to\mathbb Z_{\geq 0}$ with $h(0)>0$, the Hilbert depth of $h$ is $\operatorname{hdepth}(h)=\max\{d\;:\;\sum\limits_{j=0}^k (-1)^{k-j}\binom{d-j}{k-j}h(j)\geq 0\text{ for all }k\leq d\}$; see arXiv:2309.10521 . verdicts.title: On the Goncharov Depth Conjecture and polylogarithms of depth two
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We prove the surjectivity part of Goncharov's depth conjecture. We also show that the depth conjecture implies that multiple polylogarithms of depth $d$ and weight $n$ can be expressed via a single function $\mathrm{Li}_{n-d+1,1,\dots,1}(a_1,a_2,\dots,a_d)$, and we prove this latter statement for $d=2$.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns Goncharov's depth conjecture for multiple polylogarithms, which is a number-theoretic/motivic result unrelated to DPLL search tree depth or any 'cocomplexity function' on CNF formulas. The shared word 'depth' is purely incidental.
